_note: Walking, hiking and running trails in and near Waynesville, shown on /trails/. Every fact comes from the trail owner's own page or map (listed in `source`) and carries the date it was checked (`verified`). Fields: name, what (for readers), optional length, difficulty, surface, blaze, uses (any of walk, hike, run, bike, horse), address, website, links [{label,url}], source [urls], verified (YYYY-MM-DD). Trails in a section's optional `trails` table use name/length/difficulty/blaze only. Never guess a length, hour or rule; leave it out and point readers to the source. Not yet included because their official pages could not be checked: Fort Ancient Earthworks (Ohio History Connection site refuses automated fetches) and Spring Valley Wildlife Area (ODNR page moved; boardwalk status unconfirmed).

sections.title: Paved trail: the Little Miami Scenic Trail
sections.intro: The easiest flat, paved miles near Waynesville, good for walking, running, biking and strollers.

items.name: Little Miami Scenic Trail
items.what: A paved, multi-use rail-trail that runs about 78 miles from Beechmont Avenue in Anderson Township to Springfield, through Corwin, next to Waynesville. Towns along the way include Morrow, Oregonia, Corwin, Spring Valley, Xenia and Yellow Springs. It is part of the Buckeye Trail and the North Country National Scenic Trail. Horses are allowed in Greene County only.

items.name: Corwin trailhead
items.what: The closest trailhead to Waynesville, in the Village of Corwin. The trail map shows parking, restrooms, picnic tables and wheelchair access there. From Corwin it's 7 miles north to Spring Valley or 14.2 miles south to Morrow, so an out-and-back of any length is easy to plan.

sections.title: Caesar Creek State Park
sections.intro: Woods, lakeshore and gorge hiking on State Route 73, east of the village. Lengths, difficulty and blaze colors are from the park's official hiking map. Dogs must be leashed at all times in the park, and you should pack out what you pack in.

items.name: Caesar Creek hiking trails
items.what: Nine named hiking trails, from the 0.1-mile Bluebird Trail to the 12.1-mile Perimeter Trail around the lake. The park's hiking map shows where each one starts and where to park. Separate maps cover the mountain bike and bridle trails.

items.name: Caesar Creek mountain bike trail
items.what: Mountain bike trails with their own map. The park's map warns that parts of the trail may flood and be impassable during high water, and asks riders to stay on marked trails and call out when passing hikers.

items.name: Hisey Park
items.what: A Warren County Park District park in Corwin where nature trails wind through 158 acres of forested hillsides and floodplain wetlands, with an overlook of the Little Miami River valley. It shares a boundary with Caesar Creek State Nature Preserve for longer hikes, and the Little Miami Scenic Trail is 750 feet west of the park entrance on Middletown Road. Also a dog park, playground and first-come shelter.

items.name: Glen Helen Nature Preserve
items.what: A nature preserve in Yellow Springs. The Steps lot has more than 110 stone steps down to the beaver dam. Parking is $10 for non-members and free for members. Leashed dogs are welcome (leashes 6 feet or shorter).
items.address: 1075 State Route 343, Yellow Springs, OH 45387 (Cascades lot)
items.hours: Trails open daily, sunrise to sunset

items.name: Hazel Woods Park, Springboro
items.what: A 108-acre City of Springboro park with a paved walking path and a dog park.
